content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with mayonnaise is a ready‑to‑eat mixture of cooked or canned tuna combined with mayonnaise, often enriched with vegetables, herbs, and spices. It has a mild fish flavor, creamy texture, and can be served as a snack, side dish, or sandwich filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart and brain health.
Tuna salad with mayo is popular in the United States and Japan, where it is often served as an appetizer.
Canned tuna is typically steam‑processed, preserving most of its nutrients.
Mayonnaise gives the salad a smooth texture but also adds considerable calories and fat.
The salad is frequently used in diet plans because of its high protein content.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help reduce inflammation and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Supplies selenium and magnesium, which play roles in antioxidant defense and muscle function.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: The combination of protein and vitamins helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tuna.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Mercury
items.content: Tuna can accumulate mercury; pregnant women and children should limit consumption.

items.title: Caloric mayonnaise
items.content: Mayonnaise adds significant fat and calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tuna salad with mayo can be enjoyed on its own, spread on sandwiches, rolled in wraps, used as a filling for vegetables, or served with crackers. For extra freshness, add cucumber, onion, capers, or a squeeze of lemon juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
